Step-1.  trans-Cinnamaldehyde  
Ph-CH=CH–CHO  contains 9 C atoms (6 in Ph ring + 3 in the side chain).

Treatment with CH₃MgBr (1 → 1)  
Grignard adds CH₃ to the aldehyde carbonyl, giving the secondary alcohol  
Ph-CH=CH–CH(OH)CH₃.  
One CH₃ (1 C) is added.  
C-count: 9 + 1 = 10.

Step-2.  Oxidation with PCC (1 → 2)  
Secondary alcohol → ketone: Ph-CH=CH–COCH₃.  
No change in the number of carbons.  
C-count remains 10.

Step-3.  Johnson–Corey–Chaykovsky reaction  
(dimethyl(oxo)-λ⁶-sulfaneylidene)methane = dimethyl-sulfoxonium methylide, CH₂S(O)Me₂.  
The ylide donates one CH₂ unit to the carbonyl compound, giving an epoxide (or, by β-attack, a cyclopropane) but in either case inserts only that single CH₂.  

Thus one more carbon is incorporated: 10 + 1 = 11.

Therefore product 3 possesses 11 carbon atoms.

Answer: A
